issue: Invented habit that reads oddly: 'The summer sun even warms the cans I set out' is easily misread (trash cans?) and sun-warmed canned meals are not a canon detail (setting sec 9 leans against invented habits; his canon cooking is fire and forage, sec 3).
suggested_fix: It is. The heat ripens the berries early on the south slope; a small kindness, but I take it. Come evening I will have a sweet mouthful for the trouble.

issue: Sleeping arrangement reads as bedding down outdoors beside the fire in falling snow ('I bed down where the fire has warmed the earth'). His home is the tent (setting sec 1) and his moss bed is canon (sec 8, Green Rain line).
suggested_fix: In the tent, as always, wrapped close. My bed of moss is soft, and the ground holds the fire's warmth long into the night.

issue: Dialogue-logic slip: player says 'The rain's not letting up' and Linus answers 'It is.', which affirms the opposite polarity. Consistency problem, not canon, but it reads as a non sequitur.
suggested_fix: No, it has settled in for the evening. The autumn rain is colder than summer's, and it means business. But it feeds the mushrooms, so I forgive it its temper.

issue: Geography misnaming: 'a rainbow trout from the stream below' is wrong: the water below his camp is the lake, and per the bible he calls it 'the lake' or 'the water' in his own speech (bible geography; setting sec 4 has him fish the lake's west side). Rainbow trout in the lake in sunny summer is otherwise correct.
suggested_fix: A fine one. Berries, a few herbs, a rainbow trout from the water below for my supper. The land is generous in summer, if you know where to look.

issue: Invented recurring wildlife companion (setting sec 9, checklist 10.8): 'an owl will start up across the water; she keeps me company most fall nights' plus the follow-up 'listen for her. She is worth the waiting' establishes a personal recurring animal. Canon nature imagery must stay general. The second reply needs the same de-personalising ('listen for it').
suggested_fix: It has. The birds have said their piece for the day and gone to roost, and the slope goes quiet as the light fails. Soon an owl will start up across the water; there is usually one calling on these fall nights.

issue: Tone edges dismissive toward the townsfolk: 'Let them have their walls and their heat.' The bible bars mocking; elsewhere he explicitly does not begrudge the town (compare a-070). Mild, but softening keeps him consistent.
suggested_fix: The town holds its heat between the walls; I do not envy them today. Up here there is always a cool corner and a bit of moving air to find.

issue: Implied rain-day gathering (setting sec 4: he shelters at the tent in rain, no foraging in it): 'the rain also draws the snails out and softens the earth for digging. Every weather brings its own harvest' frames rain itself as harvest time. Secondary: snails as his harvest sits poorly since Snail is the one fish item excluded from his warm neutral-fish acceptance (sec 3).
suggested_fix: A little. But the rain softens the earth and calls up the mushrooms, and when it passes the slopes are richer for it. Every weather leaves its own harvest behind, if you meet it kindly.

issue: Non-canon forage: 'the leeks and the daisies are right at my feet'. Daisies are not a valley forage item; spring forage he knows is Leek, Daffodil, Dandelion, Wild Horseradish, Spring Onion (setting sec 3).
suggested_fix: Not far. But I do not need to see far to forage; the leeks and the daffodils are right at my feet. The fog makes the near things clearer, in its way.

issue: Foraging in the rain right now (setting sec 4: in and around his tent all day in rain, does not roam or forage in it): raining-morning context plus 'good soil under the nails is a fine way to start a morning. I gather what the wet weather brings up' puts him out digging in the rain.
suggested_fix: Not at all. The rain is softening the earth as we speak, and when it passes I will see what it has coaxed up. Until then I am content to sit dry and let it do its work.

issue: Foraging in the rain (setting sec 4): raining-morning context, player notes he is not slowed down, and 'A little rain is a friend to a forager... I have the slopes to myself' confirms he is out working the slopes in it. Fix must keep the later 'place to yourself' follow-up coherent.
suggested_fix: A little rain is a friend to a forager, though I do my picking after it passes. It brings up the mushrooms and softens the earth, and it keeps most folk indoors, so the mountain is all but mine.

issue: Dangling antecedent in the PLAYER line, not the Linus reply: 'I'm glad I did.' refers to nothing said before it. Suggested fix below is a replacement player line.
suggested_fix: I'm glad I started climbing up here.

issue: Contains 'once': 'It has never once led me astray up here.'
suggested_fix: The fog keeps its own counsel. Walk slow and it will let you through. It has never led me astray up here.

issue: Contains 'once': 'Once you have heard that sound overhead, some part of you always listens for it come autumn.'
suggested_fix: You will now. After you have heard that sound overhead, some part of you always listens for it come autumn.

issue: Contains 'once': 'It is an easy thing to love, once you let yourself slow down for it.'
suggested_fix: It is an easy thing to love, when you let yourself slow down for it. The mountain does the rest.

issue: Contains 'once': 'they have never once been late.'
suggested_fix: I know their comings and goings, more than their names. They keep no calendar but their own, and they have never been late.

issue: Contains 'once': 'never once repeats itself.'
suggested_fix: There is no finer show than a fire, my friend. It tells a different story every night and never repeats itself.

issue: Contains 'once': 'as if she never once doubted the warm days would come.'
suggested_fix: It is a sight, is it not? Every spring she throws off the grey and dresses in green, as if she never doubted the warm days would come. Each year it catches me fresh, as though I had never seen a spring before.

issue: Contains 'once': 'it always does, once the sun clears the ridge and burns it off.'
suggested_fix: The summer mist is thick this morning. It will lift soon; it always does, when the sun clears the ridge and burns it off.

issue: Contains 'once': 'I once learned to build an igloo from the tundra folk beyond the frozen sea.'
suggested_fix: I learned to build an igloo from the tundra folk beyond the frozen sea. That was many years ago.

issue: Contains 'once': 'it never once grows dull.'
suggested_fix: When you have time and quiet enough, noticing is easy. It is the great occupation of a simple life, and it never grows dull.

issue: Contains 'once': 'Try it, just once.'
suggested_fix: Try it, just one morning. Wake before the valley stirs and stand out in the cool while the light comes up. There is a peace in that first hour you will not find anywhere later in the day.

issue: Contains 'once': 'Because it is nearly always true, once you tally it honestly.'
suggested_fix: Because it is nearly always true, if you tally it honestly. A fire, a roof, a friend, and food for the morning. That is a rich man's list, if you think on it.

issue: Contains 'once': 'I have never once frozen.'
suggested_fix: The fire at my back and a heart full of wonder. Between the two, I have never frozen yet. Come, there is room; watch a while with me.

issue: Contains 'once': 'a thousand little rings blooming and vanishing at once.'
suggested_fix: You have, and I do not mind a bit. From up here I can watch the rain freckle the whole lake below, a thousand little rings blooming and vanishing together. It is a fine quiet thing to wake to.

issue: Contains 'once': 'It is harsh and it is lovely, both at once.'
suggested_fix: That is the winter's secret. It is harsh and it is lovely, both together, and it does not trouble to choose between them.

issue: Contains 'once': 'Once the dark settles in, the whole sky fills over the water.'
suggested_fix: A good day earns a close like this one. As the dark settles in, the whole sky fills over the water, one cold clear star at a time. It is a fine thing to sit with, night after night.

issue: Contains 'once': 'It is, once you stop fighting the quiet and let it in.'
suggested_fix: It is, when you stop fighting the quiet and let it in.

issue: Contains 'once': 'You should try it once.'
suggested_fix: You should try it some morning. The dawn keeps its finest gifts for the early risers.

issue: Contains 'once': 'I only give what was given to me, once, by those few who were kind.'
suggested_fix: I only give what a few kind souls gave to me, back when I most needed it. Kindness is a debt best repaid forward, to the next person who needs it.

issue: Contains 'once': 'it has never once made me regret the choosing.'
suggested_fix: With all that is left of me. I chose this place, and it has never made me regret the choosing.

issue: Contains 'once': 'like a path grassing over once you stop walking it.'
suggested_fix: It took me years to learn it. The habit of wanting wears away slow, like a path grassing over when you stop walking it.

issue: Contains 'once': 'There is freedom in that, once you find it.'
suggested_fix: Perhaps because I stopped trying to manage so much. There is freedom in that, when you find it.
